question.text: Calc: 'Yamuna Alpha Fund' (Cat III) has NAV of INR 80 crore. Long positions aggregate INR 140 crore; short positions INR 100 crore. After permissible offsetting for hedge pairs, the net offsettable amount is INR 60 crore. What is the leverage ratio under SEBI's prudential norm and is it compliant?

answer.text: Leverage = (140 + 100 - 60) / 80 = 2.25x NAV; exceeds 2x cap — NOT compliant; fund must square-off excess by end of next working day
Leverage = (140 + 100) / 80 = 3.0x; only 3x is the regulatory cap — compliant

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular CIR/IMD/DF/10/2013: Leverage = {Long positions + Short positions (after offsetting as permitted)} / NAV. Long INR 140 cr + Short INR 100 cr = INR 240 cr gross; after permissible offsetting of INR 60 cr, net exposure = INR 180 cr. INR 180 cr / INR 80 cr = 2.25x > 2x cap. Non-compliant. Fund must: report to Custodian, intimate investors before 10:00 AM next working day, square-off excess by EOD next working day. The Trap: Option B nets longs against shorts fully (wrong — only permissible hedge offsetting). Option C ignores shorts entirely. Option D invents a 3x cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests 2x numerically. XIX-C tests the offsetting mechanics and the reporting obligations on breach. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Define 'permissible offsetting' in the fund's Risk Policy — typically same-underlying hedged pairs qualify, but basis-risk or cross-asset hedges don't. NAV excludes borrowings. Breach reporting is dual: AIF->Custodian, then Custodian->SEBI by 10:00 AM next working day.
